title: Premature Data Partitioning (NUMA Node Hard-Binding)
damaged_code:
```bash
# Hard-binding task threads to specific NUMA socket 0 to "avoid bus crossing"
numactl --physcpubind=0 --membind=0 ./my_app
```
pattern: Pinning application threads and allocating memory explicitly to single NUMA CPU sockets without measuring interconnect bus traffic.
why_bad: Hard-binding threads to NUMA nodes prevents the operating system scheduler from performing effective load balancing, turning temporary workload spikes into CPU resource starvation [132, 222].
detection: Invoking NUMA-specific system configurations (`numactl` or thread affinity libraries) inside standard application deploy pipelines.
counterexample: Supercomputing cluster configurations or raw hypervisor systems running dedicated single-purpose workloads. `Contextual`.
fix: Allow the operating system kernel scheduler to dynamically allocate CPU threads and manage NUMA locality.
